rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding Mo to TiVNbTa, whereas the paper compared CrFeTaVW with Ta-substituted-by-Ti CrFeTiVW using simulations and mechanical alloying/SPS. These are different kinds of interventions (compositional doping vs. elemental substitution and processing study).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature mechanical testing at ~1273 K and 30% strain, while the paper used MD/MC simulations from 300–2100 K, SPS consolidation at 1543–1573 K, and thermal diffusivity measurements from 300–1000 K. The regimes differ entirely (mechanical loading vs. thermal diffusivity and structural simulation).
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes solid-solution strengthening and edge-dislocation slip from Mo addition, whereas the paper's mechanism involves MC-driven chemical ordering, W segregation, Laves-phase formation from Fe–Ta mixing enthalpy, and phonon mean free path effects on thermal diffusivity. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved yield/compressive strength at 1273 K, while the paper predicted and measured similar thermal diffusivity for both alloys, much lower than W/CuCrZr, and differences in phase constitution and segregation. The predicted properties and directions are unrelated.
